I've been farming this land for thirty-some years. My father farmed it before me. Here in Quzhou, everyone does wheat and maize — one after the other on the same fields. That's just how it works. The soil knows it, I know it.

I have about 10 mu. I won't try anything fancy at my age. Last time my neighbor tried cotton, he struggled with picking costs and the price dropped. I'll stay with what I understand.

**Winter wheat** goes in around mid-October. I'll use the Jimai 22 seed — it's what the supply co-op sells and it does well here. I flood-irrigate before sowing, then again at jointing and heading. Maybe once more at grain fill if it's dry. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and chase it with urea at jointing. I spray once for aphids in spring, once for powdery mildew if I see it. Rotary till before sowing.

**Summer maize** follows right after wheat harvest in June. I'll direct-seed Xianyu 335 — no need to plough, the stubble breaks down. One irrigation at silking if the sky doesn't help. I top-dress urea once at the 6-7 leaf stage. One pesticide pass for corn borer, maybe another if fall armyworm shows up like it did two years ago.

I don't overthink inputs. I apply what my neighbors apply and what the township extension station says. My yields are steady.
